newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain helped French beet crop growth, survey shows.
newsitem.headline: Rain helped French beet crop growth, survey shows.

text.p: Rain since the last week of April helped French sugar beets and crop prospects should further improve if a combination of rain and warm temperature holds, planters said on Thursday.
"At this stage there is no concern. The crop potential is intact," an analyst for the French sugar beet federation told Reuters.

A campaign survey up to May 20 shows that beet development is now in line with an average year though conditions greatly vary between regions, he said. The survey will be officially released next week.
Farmers were able to complete their sowings around March 28, some eight days ahead of an average year.
But that advantage was later lost as dry weather limited beet growth in March and early April.
"The rain has helped make up for ground lost earlier and as of May 20, crop development is now in line with an average year, give or take one day" the analyst said.
"We are now just hoping for more rain and warm weather to help accelerate crop development," he said.
The survey also showed that despite the drought the number of beets per hectare was expected to be in line with an average year, that is around 95-100,000 beets per hectare.
It also suggested that farmers may redrill 0.5 to one percent of total area sown.
Nearly four months of drought, which have depleted ground water tables, had raised concern about crop development.
But between April 25 and May 20, cumulative rainfall reached 90 mm, some 20 mm above average for that period.
Between December and mid-May, the cumulative rainfall for France's main beet-producing regions was 217 mm, still below the 30-year average of 308 mm.
